answer: The jury's own reward depends on rejecting low-quality answers, creating a shared incentive among honest graders to spot coordinated fakery, so a Sybil cluster collapses under the weight of its own low scores. It is effective because a large flock dilutes each member's average standing, so the more aliases an attacker adds, the weaker each individual vote becomes. The result is a self-purifying economy: every epoch, low-cost fake identities are filtered out by the same reputation mechanics that reward the honest ones.
